title: Tensor cohomology comparison from models of good truncations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with Grothendieck topology $J$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $B$ any commutative ring, and $R$ its constant commutative-ring sheaf, regarded as a ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $c$ for constant module presheaf sheafification along the ring unit [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $P,Q$ be K-flat cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Suppose $H^j(P)=0$ for $b_P<j$ and $H^j(Q)=0$ for $b_Q<j$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Fix an integer $i$ and an object $U$. Let $E,F$ be complexes of finite free $B$-modules, each zero in sufficiently high degrees. Suppose the standard derived category of $R|_U$-modules has isomorphisms
$$(\tau_{\ge i-b_Q}P)|_U\simeq c(E)|_U,\qquad (\tau_{\ge i-b_P}Q)|_U\simeq c(F)|_U.$$
Then, writing $T=\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_B F)$, there is an isomorphism of $R|_U$-module sheaves
$$H^i((\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q))|_U)\simeq H^i(c(T)|_U).$$
Here truncation is good lower truncation [def-kun-truncations], total tensor is the signed direct-sum total complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and restriction is to the slice site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No Noetherianity or local constancy hypothesis is imposed; the local models are supplied as data.

proof.text: Use good upper truncation and bounded-above flat replacement to represent the bounded-above derived objects with the same upper bounds on terms. They are K-flat by the bounded-above flat criterion. The mapping-cone criterion and the defining acyclic-tensor property of the given K-flat P and Q identify their tensor cohomology with that computed by these flat representatives.

Restriction is exact and commutes with sheaf tensor and sums. Restricted flat representatives remain flat and bounded above, hence K-flat. The tensor comparison is the same presheaf bilinear map at each object of the slice; slice sheafification has the same local representatives and equalities. This identifies restriction of tensor cohomology with the local derived-tensor computation.

Prove the needed truncation window directly with cutoffs a=i-bQ and c=i-bP. The removed lower pieces have upper cohomological bounds a-1 and c-1. Give each removed piece and the other factor bounded-above flat representatives using good upper truncation and bounded flat replacement. Their tensor has zero terms above the sum of these bounds, which is i-1. Tensor the truncation triangles; the long exact homology sequences therefore identify degree-i cohomology with that of the two truncated factors. A cutoff above the upper bound gives zero and is included. No separately packaged truncation-window declaration is used.

Use the two given derived isomorphisms. A finite free module realizes as a finite sum of the ring sheaf, by a basis and preservation of finite sums. Tensoring with it is a finite sum of the identity functor and is exact. Thus the constant realizations of E and F are termwise flat; their upper term bounds make them K-flat. Derived tensor descent computes their local tensor by their total tensor.

On finite free terms, the maps sending a tensor of basis vectors to the corresponding tensor-basis vector and conversely identify c(E^p) tensor c(F^q) with c(E^p tensor F^q). These maps commute with every matrix of B-linear differentials by bilinearity. If E vanishes above r and F above s, only n-s <= p <= r, q=n-p, contribute in degree n. Thus finite sums assemble the termwise comparison into an isomorphism of total complexes, including the sign (-1)^p on the second differential. Constant realization preserves these finite sums by its exactness.

Take degree-i cohomology of the complex isomorphism on the slice and combine it with the truncation and representative comparisons. Both sides are homology of restricted complexes; no commutation of restriction with homology or finite-generation assertion about cycles is included in the conclusion.

theorem site_tensor_local_model_comparison
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (B : Type u) [CommRing B]
    (P Q : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡(J, B))) ℤ)
    (hP : P.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat) (hQ : Q.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat)
    (bP bQ : ℤ)
    (hPb : ∀ j : ℤ, bP < j → IsZero (P.homology j))
    (hQb : ∀ j : ℤ, bQ < j → IsZero (Q.homology j))
    (i : ℤ) (U : C) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (SheafOfModules.{u} ((𝓡(J, B)).over U))
    ∀ (E F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ)
    (hEb : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (E.X j))
    (hFb : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (F.X j))
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Free B (E.X j) ∧ Module.Finite B (E.X j))
    (hF : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Free B (F.X j) ∧ Module.Finite B (F.X j))
    (eE : Nonempty
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            (P.truncGE (i - bQ))) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((((cB(J, B)) ⋙ overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj E)))
    (eF : Nonempty
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            (Q.truncGE (i - bP))) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((((cB(J, B)) ⋙ overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj F))),
    let T := CochainComplex.mapBifunctor E F (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (ModuleCat B))
    Nonempty
      ((((overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor P Q
            (@MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _ _ (monoidalCategory
              ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat.{u}).obj (CommRingCat.of B)))))).homology i ≅
        ((((cB(J, B)) ⋙ overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj T).homology i)
